html:
SMTO-GWT-0058 — The Gateway couldn't run the NVIDIA GPU tool

GUID: cf943235-ef0a-5702-b2bb-21f4fb6753f7
Slug: gpu-provider-unavailable
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gpu

What happened

  • SMTO uses NVIDIA's own tool (nvidia-smi) to read and change GPU settings on the Gateway computer. The Gateway couldn't find or start that tool, so the GPU action didn't complete.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the Gateway computer, open a terminal as the account that runs the Gateway and type nvidia-smi. It should print a table of your GPUs. If the tool is missing or blocked for that account, the Gateway can't use it either.
  2. If nvidia-smi is missing or fails, install or repair the NVIDIA graphics driver on that computer, which includes nvidia-smi, then restart the Gateway. The Gateway only uses the NVIDIA tool that comes with the installed driver.
  3. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Check connection for this Gateway, and confirm its GPU line says NVIDIA tools are installed. This makes SMTO re-read which GPU tools the Gateway has.
  4. If you had asked SMTO to change a GPU setting, ask it to show that GPU's details first, and request the change again only if the setting is still not what you wanted. If the tool failed partway through, the change may already have been applied.

What success looks like

  • Asking SMTO for the GPU status on this Gateway lists your GPUs without an error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with what nvidia-smi printed, to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Don't stop programs that are using the GPU to work around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's NVIDIA GPU adapter could not find nvidia-smi on PATH or hit an OS error while launching or talking to the nvidia-smi process.

What this means

  • The NVIDIA adapter could not locate nvidia-smi or caught an OS error launching or using the provider subprocess. A missing binary is one possible cause, not the only one. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • The NVIDIA adapter could not locate nvidia-smi or caught an OS error launching or using the provider subprocess. A missing binary is one possible cause, not the only one.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect provider discovery under the Gateway OS account and retained execution/effect flags before repairing installation or permissions.

How to fix it

  • On the Gateway host, confirm nvidia-smi is installed (it ships with the NVIDIA driver), is on the PATH of the account running the Gateway, and is executable by that account; run nvidia-smi as that account to check. Then select Check connection for the Gateway and run gpu.status; if a configuration change was in progress, read the device state with gpu.device before submitting another change.
  • Check nvidia-smi availability and execution permissions for the Gateway account, then inspect gpu.status. Reconcile any retained uncertain mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Install nvidia-smi on the selected Gateway and inspect gpu.status.

How to verify the fix

  • gpu.status reports usable provider access on the intended Gateway; any attempted mutation is reconciled.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, kill GPU clients automatically or invent sensor values.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
